findings.title: Build the positive release-verifier fixture from matching inventory and build bytes
findings.problem: The fixture uses current out/assets/connection-management-build.json hashes with the frozen shipped source inventory, then labels it valid. After subsequent production changes, even a fresh build fails the positive assertion at line 32, and the test never reaches the remaining negative verification matrix.
findings.observed: Current build lists 878 production files versus 875 in the inventory, with 17 changed hashes and three new files. Fresh Node22 build passes; isolated gate rerun still fails. A private synthetic inventory aligned with the exact current build passes the real source verifier.
findings.impact: The regression suite remains red after ordinary subsequent production changes, while rejecting stale shipped evidence is correct runtime behavior.
findings.recommendation: Construct a private positive inventory matching the current build, with complete private fixture classifications; use stale inventory as an explicit negative case. Keep shipped inventory/report and production release gates unchanged until real prerequisites are met.
